title: Spring Boot Exercises
description: Read each example in its lesson first. Predict the result, then check your answer. The notes explain the idea and one common mistake.

exercises.question: @RestController makes return values into HTTP responses. GET /hello calls this method. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Boot configures an HTTP server and imports the controller. GetMapping connects /hello to its returned text. A mapping must use the same path and HTTP method as the request.

exercises.question: Spring Boot writes a Map as JSON. Open GET /book. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The Map key title becomes a JSON field with value Moon Trip. JSON object field order is not part of its meaning.

exercises.question: @PathVariable reads a value from a named path position. Open GET /hello/Ravi. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The explicit path-variable name matches the placeholder. Spring passes Ravi to the method. Use the explicit input name so compilation settings do not affect binding.

exercises.question: @RequestParam reads a query value. GET /page without n uses the default 1. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The missing query input is replaced by defaultValue 1 and parsed as an int. Text that cannot become an int is rejected before this method runs.

exercises.question: An int path input is parsed by Spring. Open GET /double/4. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Spring converts the path text 4 to an int before invoking the method. The product is 8. A type checks the shape, not whether the number fits your business rule.

exercises.question: @RequestBody reads JSON into a Java record. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The JSON title is bound to the record field. Returning the record serialises that field again. A record defines fields but does not automatically make every value valid.

exercises.question: A handler can check a body value and send 400 when it is not usable. Send POST /books with {"title":"Moon Trip"}. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The title is present and not blank, so the handler returns 201 with the book body. Check input before storing or acting on it.

exercises.question: ResponseEntity lets code choose a status and body. Open GET /missing. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: ResponseEntity carries both 404 and the error object to the response writer. A failure should not use a success status just because it has a body.

exercises.question: A list becomes a JSON array. Open GET /books. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The two list items become two JSON array entries in their original order. List.of makes a list that cannot be changed in place.

exercises.question: A response can carry cache instructions. Open GET /note and inspect Cache-Control. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The response builder adds the header, then gives the response its text body. Headers need to be set before the response is sent.

exercises.question: A 302 reply with Location asks a browser to make another request. GET /start ends at /hello. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The first response has status 302 and a Location header. The browser follows it to the greeting. Redirects are client actions, not calls to another Java method.

exercises.question: @ExceptionHandler formats one error type for this controller. Open GET /broken. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The controller handler catches the declared exception type and replaces it with a controlled 500 reply. Do not expose private stack traces or internal values in error replies.
